current_evidence: The council's General Validation Advice page (last updated 8 July 2026) says 'Our validation document was adopted by Strategic Planning Committee on the 7th October 2022'; the live copy on eastdevon.gov.uk is the 'oct-22-v2' PDF (cover dated August 2019 / October 2022), while Grokbot's /media/3724737/ path now fails on the main site and survives only on the legacy azure.eastdevon.gov.uk host.

issues.detail: Grokbot's Validation list URL (eastdevon.gov.uk/media/3724737/validation-checklist-document-oct-22.pdf) no longer resolves on the council site (client error). The council now hosts the same October 2022 list as 'validation-checklist-document-oct-22-v2.pdf' under /media/pugbu2ns/. The old file is only reachable on the legacy host azure.eastdevon.gov.uk.
issues.evidence: WebFetch of workbook URL: client_error; search result: eastdevon.gov.uk/media/pugbu2ns/validation-checklist-document-oct-22-v2.pdf

issues.detail: The list date 2019-07-01 comes from PDF metadata. The document says it was first adopted on 20 August 2019 and carries an October 2022 cover date. The validation page says the current version was adopted by Strategic Planning Committee on 7 October 2022. The list date should be 2022-10-07.
issues.evidence: Validation page: 'Our validation document was adopted by Strategic Planning Committee on the 7th October 2022'; PDF para 1.5: 'formally adopted for use by East Devon District Council from the 20 August 2019'

issues.detail: The council tab holds only 8 'Drawing / document standards' fragments. Most are national location and site plan guidance or general presentation rules, cut mid-sentence with bullet glyphs left in, e.g. 'This should be an ordnance survey-based map at a standard metric scale of 1:500 or 1:200. 2.13 The plan should be up to date ... \uf0b7 \uf0b7 The scale of the plan along with a scale bar;'. None of the roughly 35 Section 3.10 local reports appear in the tab.
issues.evidence: Section 5 'Presentation of plans and drawings' and paras 2.9-2.13 (national location/site plan requirements)

issues.detail: Unilateral Undertaking / Section 111 Form is missing. It applies to all new residential development, including conversions and minor schemes, that triggers contributions towards habitat mitigation, open space or affordable housing. In practice this is one of the most common reasons East Devon applications are made invalid.
issues.evidence: 'All new residential development (including conversions) that generate the need for financial contributions ... towards habitat mitigation (or alternatively a Unilateral Undertaking)'

issues.detail: Sustainable Drainage Strategy is missing. Its trigger is residential development of 10 or more units, other development of 1,000 sqm or more, or any development in a Critical Drainage Area, and outline applications have a separate checklist. Grokbot's 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' row instead repeats the Foul Drainage Assessment trigger (no mains connection / source protection zones).
issues.evidence: 'Residential development of 10 or more units and other development of 1000sqm or more floorspace; Development within Critical Drainage Areas.'

issues.detail: Several other local requirements are missing: (1) Green Infrastructure Plan, required for major full applications with strategic landscaping (major housing, employment, solar farms) and major outline applications where landscaping is being discharged; (2) Economic Impact Assessment, required for major applications involving loss of land or buildings last used for employment, retail or community purposes; (3) Marketing Strategy Statement, required for all applications proposing loss of commercial or community facilities; (4) Foul Sewerage and Utilities Assessment, required for all large scale major development; (5) Street Scenes, required for works visible from a road for new buildings or large extensions.
issues.evidence: Section 3.8 Street Scenes; Section 3.10 reports list (Green Infrastructure Plan, Economic Impact Assessment, Marketing Strategy Statement, Foul Sewerage and Utilities Assessment)

issues.detail: The Section 4 'Additional Local Requirements for Listed Building Consent' are almost entirely missing. They set out what to submit for thatching, re-roofing in slate/tile, replacement windows (joinery sections at 1:2 or 1:5), render, shopfronts, internal alterations, new flues/vents/extractors/chimneys, and demolition for structural reasons. Grokbot only has a 'Photographs / Photomontages' row built from a fragment of the flues text.
issues.evidence: Section 4: thatching, re-roofing, replacement windows, render, shopfronts, internal alterations, flues/vents, demolition for structural reasons

issues.detail: The CIL Additional Information Form appears only under Full planning, and Reserved matters, Lawful development cert and Variation of condition s73 are all marked '(none)'. The source requires the form for householder applications over 100 sqm of new floorspace, reserved matters for CIL-liable uses, lawful development certificates, s73 variations adding chargeable floorspace, conversions, changes of use to residential/retail, and new-build annexes.
issues.evidence: 'Householder applications over 100sqm ...; Reserved Matters applications following outline permission ...; Applications for lawful development certificates; Application for a variation of condition if additional chargeable floorspace is proposed; ... New build annexes'

issues.detail: About 25 rows carry the note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning', while Outline and Reserved matters are marked '(none)'. The source applies many of these by scale or location, not to full applications only. Examples: Tree Survey/AIA explicitly covers 'Major Full, Outline or Reserve Matters' and minor applications; Flood Risk Assessment covers all development in Flood Zones 2 and 3 including minor development and householder schemes; Green Infrastructure has an outline framework variant; the SuDS checklist has an outline version; Heritage Statement and Biodiversity Survey also apply to householder and listed building works.
issues.evidence: Tree Survey section: 'Major Full, Outline or Reserve Matters applications'; FRA: 'All development in Flood Zones 2 and 3 including minor development and changes of use.'

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment trigger quotes only the first bullet ('All development of 1 hectare of more in Flood Zone 1'). It leaves out the main local triggers: development in Critical Drainage Areas, sites under 1 ha in Flood Zone 1 with a change to a more vulnerable use, and all development in Flood Zones 2 and 3.
issues.evidence: 'Development in a critical drainage areas; less than 1 ha in flood zone 1, including a change of use ... All development in Flood Zones 2 and 3 including minor development and changes of use.'

issues.detail: Some requirements are mislabelled. 'Housing mix / dwelling standards (NDSS, accessible homes)' is actually the Health Impact Statement trigger (residential over 100 units and other large scale major development), and the list has no NDSS requirement. 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details' is actually the Site Waste Management Plan (construction waste, large scale major only). 'Biodiversity Checklist / Questionnaire' is actually the Biodiversity Survey and Report, and its trigger leaves out the designated-site (SSSI, SAC, LNR, etc.) and site clearance / demolition of older buildings or roof spaces triggers.
issues.evidence: '27 Health Impact Statement ... Residential development over 100 units'; '39 Site Waste Management Plan ... All large scale major planning applications'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are garbled or cut off. Some start with the tail of the previous section ('question. 48', 'Levy. 19', 'more. 14', 'Directive. 51') and keep the raw \uf0b7 bullet glyphs. Others are meaningless fragments: Advertisement drawings 'levels of luminance and glare.', Lighting 'amount of external lighting.', Sunlight to gardens 'gardens and amenity space.', EIA 'require an Environmental Impact Assessment.' The Structural Survey trigger ('may be required for any extensive alterations') misses the source triggers, which are barn conversions and significant demolition or rebuilding of listed buildings.
issues.evidence: Structural Survey: barn conversions; significant demolition/rebuilding of listed buildings

issues.detail: 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' and 'Foul Sewage / Utilities Statement' both use the same Foul Drainage Assessment (FDA1) trigger. 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' is a fragment of the Daylight/Sunlight Assessment row. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' is a fragment of the Lighting Report, and the list has no advertisement-specific requirement.
issues.evidence: '23 Foul Drainage Assessment ... Cases where it is not possible to connect to existing foul drainage facilities'

issues.detail: This is a source issue, not a Grokbot error. The October 2022 list is more than two years old even though para 1.5 commits to a two-yearly review. It does not mention statutory Biodiversity Net Gain (mandatory from Feb 2024) or Fire Statements, and it still uses the pre-2020 A3/A4/A5 use classes. Users should check BNG and other national requirements separately.
issues.evidence: Para 1.5: 'this document will be reviewed at least every 2 years'; no BNG section

summary: Grokbot's link is now broken on the council site; the current list is the same October 2022 local list re-hosted as 'oct-22-v2', and the list date (2019 metadata) is wrong. Content capture is weak: the tab holds only plan-presentation fragments, key local items are missing (Unilateral Undertaking/S111, SuDS, Green Infrastructure, listed building Section 4 details), CIL and other items are wrongly limited to Full planning, and several triggers are mislabelled or truncated.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
